criteria.text: Calculates the long-stop date as 28 April 2027 (150 days after signing on 29 November 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 12 June 2027 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies the conflict between the 30-day claim notice period in SPA Section 9.7 and the 45-day period in Escrow Clause 5.2, and recommends the Buyer works to the shorter 30-day period or aligns the documents.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.

Identifies that the core platform was developed by contractor Redcliffe Logistics plc without a written IP assignment, so the Company may not own it, and recommends obtaining a confirmatory assignment as a condition to Closing.

Identifies the threatened $1,200,000 claim by Bellhaven Pharma plc recorded in the board minutes and that it is not disclosed against the litigation warranty (Warranty 7.1), recommending a specific indemnity or price protection.
Gives the long-stop period as 150 days and as the date 28 April 2027, with days remaining from 7 December 2026 (142 days).
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
Opens with a short 'Bottom line' / executive summary stating the overall conclusion and the most important risks before the detailed analysis.
